### ui/perf-graph.js
Compact, stackable, canvas-rendered performance graph as a <perf-graph> custom element. One element = one scrolling metric strip (frame time, fps, heap, any numeric gauge): push(value) appends a sample, the newest sample hugs the right edge, history scrolls left. Every pixel — including all text (label, current value, avg/min/max readout, tick labels) — is drawn on one shadow-DOM <canvas> via fillText: zero DOM text nodes, no layout, no dependencies. Redraws only when new data / size / theme. Arrive (dirty flag, at most one rAF pending, none when idle) and skips drawing fully while the tab is hidden or the element is scrolled out of view (one deferred draw on becoming visible). DPR-aware backing store (crisp on HiDPI), when samples outnumber plot pixels the trace switches from a polyline (+ soft area fill) to per-pixel min-max columns via binMinMax.

Steady-state draws allocate nothing. Re-exports everything from ui/perf-graph-math.js so one import is enough.

Importing the module auto-registers <perf-graph> (unless that tag is taken).

  import '.../ui/perf-graph.js';

  <perf-graph label="frame" unit="ms" budget="16.7"></perf-graph>

Element <perf-graph> attributes (all optional. Properties mirror them, and property setters reflect back to the attributes). Label — name drawn top-left unit — 'ms' (default) | 'fps' | any custom suffix | '' for bare numbers history — samples kept/displayed (default 240). Changing it live preserves the newest samples height — element height in CSS px (default 48. This also covers compact) min/max — fixed scale ends. This also covers omit either for autoscale (autoRange + nice 1-2-5 gridlines, range quantized so ticks stay put) budget — guide value (e.g. 16.7) drawn as a dashed amber line, always kept inside the displayed range

Element properties / methods: push(value: number) — append one sample. Schedules (at most) one rAF redraw clear() — drop all samples refreshTheme() — re-read the --perf-graph-* custom properties label, unit, history, height. Reflected properties for the attributes min, max, budget: number | null (null = attribute absent)

CSS custom properties (read via getComputedStyle, cached. Dark Scratch Proto defaults, set on the element, an ancestor, or :root): --perf-graph-bg. Background (#0d0f14) --perf-graph-line — trace / columns (#00e47a) --perf-graph-fill — area fill under the polyline. 'none' disables (rgba(0, 228, 122, 0.10)) --perf-graph-grid — gridlines (rgba(200, 205, 216, 0.08)) --perf-graph-text. It label/stats/ticks (#6b7280) --perf-graph-value, current-value readout (#e8ecf4) --perf-graph-budget. Budget line (#f0a500) --perf-graph-font — canvas font family ('JetBrains Mono', 'SF Mono', 'Cascadia Code', 'Fira Code', monospace) --perf-graph-font-size — base font size in px (10)

Stacked HUD example — several graphs sit flush in a plain column (:host is display:block, width:100%, margin-free), all fed from one rAF loop:

  <div id="hud" style="position: fixed; top: 0; right: 0; width: 260px;">
    <perf-graph id="ft"  label="frame" unit="ms"  budget="16.7"></perf-graph>
    <perf-graph id="fps" label="fps"   unit="fps" min="0" max="120"></perf-graph>
    <perf-graph id="mem" label="heap"  unit="MB"  history="600" height="32"></perf-graph>
  </div>

  import '.../ui/perf-graph.js';
  const ft = document.getElementById('ft');
  const fps = document.getElementById('fps');
  const mem = document.getElementById('mem');
  let last = performance.now();
  requestAnimationFrame(function tick(now) {
    const dt = now - last;
    last = now;
    ft.push(dt);
    fps.push(1000 / dt);
    if (performance.memory) mem.push(performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize / 2 ** 20);
    requestAnimationFrame(tick);
  });

Exports. Class PerfGraphElement extends HTMLElement Exported so you can register under another name: customElements.define('my-graph', PerfGraphElement) THEME_DEFAULTS. The default theme values keyed like the properties Plus everything (CSS) re-exported from ui/perf-graph-math.js.

### ui/perf-graph-math.js
The graph's pure math. No DOM or browser APIs (unit-tested under node). Hot paths are allocation-free — the ring allocates only on construction / setCapacity, and computeStats/binMinMax fill caller-owned outputs.

Exports: class SampleRing Fixed-capacity float32 ring buffer: constructor(capacity), push(v), at(i) (0 = oldest. NaN out of range), latest() (NaN when empty), clear(), setCapacity(n) (preserves the newest samples), getters length / capacity. Capacity clamps to >= 1. computeStats(ring, out: PerfStats) → PerfStats Fills the caller-owned { current, avg, min, max } (returns it). Non-finite samples are skipped for avg/min/max. All fields NaN when empty.

Current is the raw latest sample. autoRange(dataMin, dataMax, opts?: AutoRangeOptions) → Padded display range (DisplayRange) { min, max }. opts: fixedMin/fixedMax pin an end exactly, pad (default 0.1) pads. Each free end by pad × span, includeZero extends a free end to 0 (a zero floor from non-negative data is not padded below 0). Degenerate-safe: empty/flat data still yields a usable nonzero span. niceStep(span, maxTicks) → number Smallest 1-2-5 × 10^k step splitting span into <= maxTicks intervals. niceTicks(lo, hi, maxTicks) → number[] Tick positions on that grid within [lo, hi] (at most maxTicks + 1.

[] for an invalid range). Allocates — call only when the range moves. binMinMax(ring, bins, outMin: Float32Array, outMax: Float32Array) → number Min-max downsample for more-samples-than-pixels: sample i lands in bin floor(i * bins / count). Every finite sample influences exactly one bin and outMin[b] <= outMax[b]. Empty bins are NaN. Bins clamps to the out arrays.

Returns the number of non-empty bins. formatValue(v, unit) → string Deterministic readout formatting: non-finite → '—'. This also covers 'ms' → adaptive decimals (|v| >= 100 → 0, >= 10 → 1, else 2) + 'ms'. This also covers 'fps' → rounded + 'fps'. Other non-empty unit → 1 decimal + suffix. '' → bare adaptive number.

Types: PerfStats, AutoRangeOptions, DisplayRange

### ui/timeline-view.js
Canvas-rendered realtime swimlane timeline as a <timeline-view> custom element. A shared horizontal time axis across the full width, stacked labeled lanes (left gutter, ellipsized labels, full text via tooltip. Lane order = exactly the order supplied — never re-sorted internally), each a band of interval bars (left = start, right = end). A lane grows extra sub-tracks when intervals VISIBLE in the current window overlap, and rows are VERTICALLY STICKY (a stateful per-lane TrackAllocator). An interval KEEPS its row while it stays on screen, panning and live updates never reshuffle the rows being watched. An interval scrolling out and back gets its old row back when still free (bounded LRU row memory.

The memory survives setData. A live resync leaves rows put), and new arrivals take the lowest conflict-free row. Lane height recovers from the bottom once a tall burst scrolls away (never by re-rowing what is still visible). A historical parallelism burst stops padding its lane once it scrolls out of view, a lane with nothing visible collapses to one track. It height changes ease over ~150ms (snapped under prefers-reduced-motion. Hit-testing tracks the animating layout).

AUTO-FIT (default on.

Opt out with the no-auto-fit attribute): when the natural stack — every lane at --timeline-track-height. This is will overflow the host's height, whole lanes are demoted to the compact track height (--timeline-track-height-compact, a later default CSS px. The canvas' DPR scaling supplies device. Pixels) one at a time. Tallest (most parallel) lane first — ties demote the LOWER lane first, so top-of-chart lanes keep detail longest — until the stack fits. Otherwise, every lane is compact (only then does vertical lane scrolling engage, as before).

Demotion is immediate. Re-promotion needs ~10% height headroom (hysteresis — heights cannot flap at the boundary), the demotion set re-derives from the visible window each pass (a parallelism burst scrolling away hands its demotion to the now-tallest lane, deterministically). And demotion/promotion rides the same ~150ms height tween. Compact slivers stay legible. Bars keep the 2px minimum width and a border capped to the sliver, pips shrink but never below a 4px-tall diamond. In-bar labels are suppressed below fit height, and gutter labels degrade gracefully (full → smaller/faded → skipped below ~10px lane height, where the gutter tooltip still names the lane) without ever overlapping a neighbor.

Read fitState / listen for 'fitchange' to observe the demotion set. Everything is data — lanes, intervals, optional connectors between intervals, vertical time markers. Dynamic lane count (1-50+), smooth with thousands of in-window intervals (viewport culling, dirty-flag rAF drawing. DPR-aware backing store capped at 3, adaptive idle pacing. This is full rate while interacting + a ~500ms grace, ~30fps idle, ~10fps idle on battery. This holds via navigator.getBattery feature-detection, paused while the document is hidden.

Those tier rates are a CEILING. Device px per second) — the rAF loop keeps running and skips frames that will be pixel-identical, on an even frame-aligned cadence (clockDrawBudgetMs. Do this while the only motion is clock-driven (the follow-now scroll, ongoing-bar growth) the effective rate is min(tier fps. Never timer wakes. Motion stays smooth at every zoom, and at normal zooms the px rate meets the tier so pacing is exactly. The tier's) — and a chart with nothing animating draws nothing at all.

Input/data/hover changes still render immediately via the dirty flag). Canvas text is kept crisp. The 2d context is OPAQUE (alpha: false — the chart paints its own background every frame. An opaque canvas gets subpixel text antialiasing where an alpha one gets grayscale-only. Keep --timeline-bg an opaque color), and every TEXT draw origin snaps to the device-pixel grid (labels step in whole pixels. This happens while lanes tween/scroll — deliberate.

This also covers grid-aligned glyphs beat smeared ones). Rendering is stability-first. The viewport origin is snapped to whole DEVICE pixels once per frame and nothing else on the time axis is rounded (text origins are the one per-element exception — nothing tiles against a label). Follow-mode scrolling translates the whole scene in integer device-pixel steps and bars never jiggle relative to each other. The now line is the VIEWPORT-anchored element. Its x is computed from the RAW view (nowLineX).

This is never the snapped render view, whose per-frame quantization error used to wiggle the line. Between adjacent device pixels — so while follow-now is engaged it holds perfectly still as the scene scrolls under it. Hatch/stipple pattern fills are phase-anchored to the CONTENT they fill (a span's unclamped origin, a coverage gap's start), not to the canvas. The texture travels 1:1 with its span instead of the span sliding over a static screen-space pattern. Not a Gantt (many bars per row), not a flame chart (no nesting).

Color encodes CATEGORY: interval.category (default lane.group, then laneId) hashes to a stable hue, same category = same color, forever. With a small deterministic tone offset so near hues still separate. Rendering STYLE encodes state/phase. Via a named style map. interval.state and segment.kind look up a treatment. The treatment fields: pattern solid|hatch|stipple|outline, alphaScale, saturationScale, lightnessScale, border {width, dash, emphasis}.

The glyph field is none|bang|dot, dimmed. Built-ins: '' solid, 'emphasis'/'failed' unmissable (2px emphasis border + corner bang glyph + stipple — hue untouched). 'dim'/'queued' translucent + desaturated, 'hatch'/'waiting' 45-degree stripes.

'outline' hollow. 'cancelled' hollow + DASHED category-hue border. Unmissably "stopped, not failed" at any zoom: never the emphasis color, not the bang. Not a solid success body (a BAR's border dash falls back to solid below ~12px width, where dashes read as broken corners. The hollow body still separates a tiny cancelled bar from a solid one. This solid-below-legibility rule applies to any dashed border style on bars.

Instant PIPS are exempt. A cancelled pip keeps its dashed diamond outline — the declared pattern is rescaled so 3-5 whole dash cycles close around the perimeter. So a cancelled instant carries the same dashed signature as a cancelled span). A style with `dimmed: true` (the dim/queued/hatch/waiting built-ins) renders as ONE uniform filter over the region's GEOMETRY: fill, hatching, and border all get the same dimColor transform (50% saturation, 50% value — hue and alpha untouched). The section reads quieter than a running span. Label and badge text is deliberately EXEMPT from that filter.

Every span-surface label (bar labels, adapter-composed badge strings like queue ordinals) always renders at the full-contrast foreground (--timeline-fg) over a thin counter-color halo (labelHaloColor: dark rim under a light fg, light rim under a dark one). Text stays readable over solid, dimmed, hatched, and mixed surfaces at EVERY zoom. Deriving text color from the section underneath produced unreadable grey-on-grey labels. Those labels flipped with the zoom level as the label's anchor crossed segment boundaries. Ongoing intervals (end == null) render to the live now edge with a subtly pulsing leading edge (static under prefers-reduced-motion. While the feed is STALE they freeze at the last vouched timestamp and restyle dim + hatched — see Feed staleness below).

Zero/near-zero-DURATION intervals (mapped width under ~3px at the current zoom) render as instant diamond pips at their start time. Distinct from bars, still category-colored, state-styled (a failed instant gets the thick emphasis border + stem), hoverable and clickable via a widened hit target. The bar-vs-pip decision comes from the DURATION mapped through the scale (durationWidthPx) — translation-invariant, so shapes never flicker while the timeline scrolls. A real-duration bar is clamped to MIN_BAR_PX (2px), not demoted to a pip.

Instant markers CLUSTER at scale. Pips whose centers will visually overlap in the current window (within ~12px of a neighbor — a greedy transitive sweep, re-derived per layout pass) merge into ONE point-like STACKED marker. This is the SAME diamond pip as a single instant. The SAME diamond pip is drawn as a stack of multiple copies (ghost copies offset straight RIGHT behind the true front. Pip with a depth fade — front full-bright, middle dimmer, back dimmest. Always three, not scaled by the member count — the stack silhouette alone says "several live here", and there is no count text on the canvas.

The tooltip carries the real ×N count. Membership is exactly "would visually overlap". A stacked pip can only ever BE a cluster) — never a duration bar. An instantaneous event has no length, and neither does a pile of them. The cluster packs as ONE row slot spanning its member extent, so a burst of coincident instants cannot blow up the lane height. Membership depends only on time deltas and the scale, so panning never re-clusters (no jitter — the marker sits at the member extent's midpoint, sliding along the visible slice at a window edge instead of hiding off-screen).

This holds while ZOOMING IN progressively splits every cluster until each pip stands at its true timestamp.

A cluster styles by its members' shared state where uniform (an all-'dim' cluster stays dim-flavored. Mixed states fall back to the neutral default) and hits as {type. 'cluster', intervals, lane}: hovering shows a COMPONENT-BUILT summary tooltip (count, time extent, a bounded number of member labels then '+K more', a zoom hint) — tooltipFor is never consulted for clusters. It clicking ZOOMS to the member extent (centered, ~60% fill, min-span floored) so the cluster splits, instead of dispatching intervalclick. Fully coincident members zoom to the minimum span and stay one marker (they genuinely share a timestamp — the tooltip lists them). Ongoing intervals and real-duration bars never cluster.

Single pips keep exact tooltipFor/intervalclick behavior.

Spans CLIPPED by the viewport carry an edge-continuation cue. The clipped end darkens into a SHADOW over the last ~12px. Toward that edge, black at the edge itself, darker than the background, easing to clear inward, plus a 1px near-black boundary line. The span reads as sliding UNDER the window edge, which covers it and casts a shadow on it (never a fade to the background: that made the span look like it evaporates there). Applies left when the true start is scrolled off-screen, right when the true end — or an ongoing bar's extent in a parked view. Exceeds the window, over every treatment (solid, hollow, hatched, terminal cuts).

Spans whose edge coincides with the window edge are exempt (they genuinely start/end there), as are stubs too short to reach through the shadow zone (which will swallow them). Bar labels truncate with an ellipsis. Bar labels are suppressed below fit width — they never spill into neighboring bars. Stick to the plot edge while a bar's start is scrolled off-screen ( past the continuation shadow when one is active).

A MINIMAP strip (32px, its own canvas) runs along the bottom while data exists. The FULL loaded extent, earliest loaded interval widened by coverage knowledge (first covered time, the exhausted-history boundary) through max(now, latest end). As per-lane collapsed density marks in category hues at low alpha (no text. Sub-pixel runs stay ≥1px so piles read as density). A now tick (muted while stale), and the current viewport as a brighter window rect with grabbable LEFT/RIGHT handles. Dragging a handle adjusts that window edge live (clamped to the extent and the ~2s..~7d span limits, dragging one handle past the other CLAMPS at the minimum span, and never flips).

Dragging the middle pans the window at constant width (1:1 under the pointer, clamped inside the extent). Clicking the strip outside the window centers the window there and continues as a grab. Handle hit zones are generous (~8px, reaching outside the rect but shrinking inside so even a narrow window keeps a grabbable middle. The window rect itself never draws under ~6px). Minimap gestures go through the SAME view semantics as canvas gestures: a middle/right-handle drag is pan-like (backward disengages follow. Docking at the live edge re-engages), the left handle is zoom-like (a pinned live edge stays pinned), and moving into uncovered past fires loadRange exactly like panning there.

The strip repaints only when the main chart draws (same rAF loop, same idle pacing). It hides — ceding its band back to the plot — when there is no data. This happens when the host is shorter than ~140px, or with the no-minimap attribute. The plot canvas, lane packing, auto-fit, tooltip clamps. The plot hit-testing all size against the remaining plot area automatically, and the corner buttons ride up above the strip. Fullscreen and the minimap compose (the strip stays at the bottom of the filled viewport).

Importing the module auto-registers <timeline-view> (unless the tag is taken).

  import '.../ui/timeline-view.js';

  <timeline-view id="tl" style="height: 400px"></timeline-view>

  const tl = document.getElementById('tl');
  const now = Date.now();
  tl.setData({
    lanes: [
      { id: 'build-queue', label: 'build queue' },
      { id: 'deploy-queue', label: 'deploy queue', group: 'deploys' },
    ],
    intervals: [
      { id: 'j1', laneId: 'build-queue', start: now - 300_000, end: now - 120_000,
        label: 'job #17', category: 'build',
        segments: [{ start: now - 300_000, end: now - 240_000, kind: 'queued' }] },
      { id: 'j2', laneId: 'build-queue', start: now - 100_000, end: now - 100_000,
        label: 'skipped', category: 'build', state: 'dim' },     // instant pip
      { id: 'j3', laneId: 'deploy-queue', start: now - 90_000, end: null,
        label: 'deploy #4', category: 'deploy' },                 // ongoing
      { id: 'j4', laneId: 'deploy-queue', start: now - 200_000, end: now - 150_000,
        label: 'deploy #3', category: 'deploy', state: 'failed' },
    ],
    connectors: [{ fromIntervalId: 'j1', toIntervalId: 'j3', label: 'triggers' }],
    markers: [{ time: now - 150_000, label: 'config change', kind: 'emphasis' }],
    coverage: { start: now - 300_000, end: now },
  });
  tl.loadRange = async (start, end) => {
    const rows = await fetch(`/api/history?from=${start}&to=${end}`).then(r => r.json());
    tl.mergeData({ intervals: rows });
    return { exhausted: rows.length === 0 };
  };
  tl.addEventListener('intervalclick', (e) => showDetails(e.detail.interval));

Element <timeline-view> — data API (properties/methods, do not attributes): setData({lanes?, intervals?, connectors?, markers?, coverage?}) Replace all data. coverage: {start, end} declares the time range the supplied intervals fully cover (async-history bookkeeping). mergeData(data) — merge into the current set: lanes/intervals dedupe by id (intervals replace in place), connectors by (from, to, kind), markers by (time, label, kind). How loadRange results are supplied. setLanes(lanes) / setIntervals(intervals) / setConnectors(connectors) / setMarkers(markers) — replace one slice of the data. clear() — drop everything. markFresh(ts?) — stamp the live feed fresh without merging data (setData/mergeData stamp automatically.

See Feed staleness below). staleAfterMs — staleness threshold (see Feed staleness below). legendEntries — TimelineLegendEntry[] {glyph, text}: consumer rows appended under the built-in vocabulary in the "?" legend panel. How a consumer explains glyphs it composes into LABELS (queue-position badges like '⧗ group · 3rd', holder counts like '⏳N'). Copied on set. An open panel re-renders immediately.

colorFor — (interval, lane) => cssColor | null override. tooltipFor — (hit: TimelineHit) => string | Node | null. This also covers null/ undefined hides. Default tooltip shows label, category, state, start/end, duration, segment durations. Node content is appended, not innerHTML. Long lines WRAP inside the box (unbroken tokens like run ids/error blobs included.

Newlines in string content are honored). Pathological content clips at a max height instead of outgrowing the host — nothing ever spills past the tooltip border. NEVER called for cluster hits — their summary tooltip is component-built (see instant clustering above). loadRange — (start, end) => Promise<{exhausted?: boolean} | void>. Invoked (one request at a time, min-chunk widened. A rejected load is retried on a fixed ~2s cadence forever.

No growing backoff, no try cap, no give-up, and the uncovered hatching stays visible while it keeps trying) when the viewport reaches uncovered past. BACKWARD history only: requests never reach past the covered end, so the sliver between the last covered time. The live "now" is never asked for. Keep coverage.end current via setData/mergeData `coverage` on every live update (a live feed owns the forward edge. loadRange can then never chase the advancing clock and refire per round-trip). With no coverage at all, one bootstrap request may reach "now" and latches once settled.

Uncovered regions draw hatched (with 'loading…' while in flight) — visually distinct from covered-but-empty. {exhausted: true} pins a dashed 'history ends here' boundary with a darkened void. Before it and stops further requests. nowProvider — () => msSinceEpoch override for replay/testing. fitState — read-only {enabled: boolean, demoted: laneId[]}: the current auto-fit demotion set in display order (mirrors the latest 'fitchange' event).

Interval shape: {id, laneId, start, end?, label?, category?, state?, segments?, data?}. start/end are ms since epoch or Date. End null/ undefined = ongoing. segments: [{start, end?, kind}] phases WITHIN the bar, each styled via kind (e.g. a dim leading 'queued' phase, a hatched 'waiting' span). End null = to the bar's end. A segment whose kind resolves to the 'outline' pattern is a TERMINAL CUT (e.g. a kill tail: cancel requested → finished). It renders as a dark scrim over the dead tail — plus, once the tail is >= ~4px wide, a cut line. That line is in the segment's own hue (the cancelled border's color family) marking the kill point.

Hairline tails stay scrim-only, because a lone line flush against the span's end border reads as a stray artifact — and NEVER vanishes. It keeps a >= 3-device-px footprint (grown backward from its end) at any zoom, unlike decorative phases. These skip below half a pixel. data is opaque and echoed back in events/tooltips. Connector: {fromIntervalId, toIntervalId, kind?, label?} — a muted S-curve between multiple bars, endpoint-dotted, highlighted on hover. This also covers if one endpoint id is missing from the data a dashed stub + open circle marks it. The tooltip says which side is not loaded.

Marker: {time, label?, kind?} — dashed vertical line. This also covers kind 'emphasis' renders in the emphasis color.

Viewport / follow: viewport — getter {start, end} (ms). DEFAULT window. Until the first user gesture or setViewport call, the visible span is ASPECT-DERIVED. A few minutes at a 16:9 container, scaled linearly by the host's actual aspect ratio (defaultSpanForAspect, clamped ~2s..~7d), ending at now. Re-derived on every host resize, END anchored, while still untouched. Any gesture or setViewport latches the window as CHOSEN and the default never applies again.

followNow / jumpToNow move position only and do NOT latch. Consumers that call setViewport keep their own initial window fully. setViewport(start, end) — explicit window (span clamped ~2s..~7d. Hard-stops at now. Engages follow only when it ends within the 2-device-px snap zone of now. Latches the window as chosen — see DEFAULT window).

followNow — boolean (default true): right edge pinned to live now. Any backward PAN (wheel, drag, arrow keys) disengages immediately — even a tiny step, so trackpad panning escapes the pin. ZOOMS never inherit the pin. The anchor is ALWAYS the gesture's focal point (cursor / pinch midpoint / keyboard center), even while following — during the gesture the timestamp under the cursor stays under the cursor. The zoomed view re-earns follow by the same snap rule as any fresh gesture (zooming AT the live edge keeps following. An anchored zoom-in away from it parks, and follow re-docks magnetically on a later gesture).

One deliberate asymmetry: a zoom-out pinned at the live edge cannot show the future. The end stop caps it right-anchored — the same clamp a parked zoom-out hits at the stop. User-driven views HARD-STOP at now (every pan/zoom/pinch/keyboard/setViewport clamps the right edge there), and a gesture parking the right edge. A bounded number of DEVICE pixels of that end stop re-engages follow. It drags to the stop re-docks reliably, while a view parked merely NEAR the edge (3+ device px) stays put. The small follow lead (FOLLOW_LEAD_FRAC = 2% of span ahead of the now line) is EASED, not assigned: engaging keeps the view exactly where the gesture parked and glides the lead in over ~200ms.

Disengaging lets the backward deltas consume the lead, any residual gliding out the same way — the view never teleports in a single frame (prefers-reduced-motion snaps instead).

jumpToNow(). Re-engage follow, keeping the span. A fast ~250ms glide from wherever the view is to the followed position, not a teleport (reduced motion snaps). fullscreen        — boolean property, reflected as the `fullscreen` attribute. Viewport-fill mode. The host goes position:fixed inset:0 over the whole viewport (deliberately NOT the Fullscreen API — no permission prompt. The :host([fullscreen]) rules are !important so they beat page styles sizing the host).

The page scroll locks while active (html overflow hidden, previous value restored — the page's scroll offset survives the round trip exactly), and everything re-derives through the normal resize path (the DPR cap stays at 3). Escape exits (handled only while fullscreen — never swallowed otherwise). A corner ⤢/⤡ toggle button sits at bottom-right, visible in BOTH follow and parked modes (the jump-to-live pill slides in to its left). Hide the button with the no-fullscreen-button attribute (the property and attribute keep working programmatically). Events. 'viewportchange' {start, end, followNow} on user-driven changes, 'intervalclick' {interval, lane} (single intervals only — a cluster click zooms to its member extent instead), 'intervalhover' {interval|null, lane|null}, 'connectorclick' {connector}, 'laneclick' {lane} (a click on a gutter label — lets consumers make lanes navigable), 'fitchange' {demoted: laneId[]}.

This happens when auto-fit's demotion set changes, 'stalechange' {stale, lastFresh} on feed-staleness transitions, 'fullscreenchange' {fullscreen} on viewport-fill transitions. A built-in jump-to-live pill appears while not following (hide it with the no-live-pill attribute).

Legend (the "?" pill): a small button stacked above the fullscreen toggle opens an in-place glyph dictionary — the component-owned vocabulary (filled/hollow instant pips, the stacked cluster pip, the failed stipple + bang, hatched wait/queued phases, dim de-emphasis, the cancelled span's dashed hollow + terminal kill cut). Any consumer `legendEntries` follows that cut. Rows name a GLYPH and its meaning — nothing meta — and cover only glyphs that are actually cryptic: self-explanatory chrome (the minimap, edge treatments) stays out. Pure DOM chrome in the shadow root. It works in fullscreen, costs the nothing of the canvas render path (rows build only when the panel opens), swatches are CSS-drawn. In a neutral hue (they teach shape, not any category color), Escape or any chart gesture closes it (inside fullscreen, Escape closes the panel first, then the mode).

The no-legend attribute hides the pill fully.

Feed staleness (a dead live feed is impossible to misread): Every setData/mergeData stamps the feed FRESH. markFresh(ts?) stamps explicitly — call it from polls that returned "no changes" so a quiet-but-healthy feed never reads as stale. When staleAfterMs (default 10_000. Tune to ~2 poll intervals. 0 or a non-finite value disables, use that for static, loaded-once datasets) passes without a stamp. The chart goes STALE instead of extrapolating dead data: the live edge.

Ongoing (end=null) bar ends, the now line, the follow pin, the forward clamp on user views. FREEZES at the last vouched timestamp (a finished 5s run whose end never arrived shows ~5s, and never "running forever"), ongoing bars restyle as unknown (dimmed + hatch overlay, no pulse), the now line goes muted + dashed. A built-in "live data stale (Ns) — reconnecting…" note counts up forever (fixed cadence, and never gives up). 'stalechange' {stale: true, lastFresh} fires. A followed view stops scrolling (the frozen content never slides out of view). The next stamp exits stale mode and the live edge GLIDES back to the real clock (~250ms.

Composes with the follow pin — no teleport on recovery either. Reduced motion snaps). On 'stalechange' back to fresh, consumers must do ONE full resync (setData) before resuming incremental merges — runs that ended during the outage otherwise stay unknown. A full setData mid-stale is handled gracefully and recovers in the same call. staleState — read-back getter {stale, lastFresh}.

Attributes (scalar toggles only): no-live-pill, no-auto-fit (disable compact-lane auto-fit — every lane keeps the full track height), history-end-text (boundary label, default 'history ends here'), empty-text (empty-state hint), fullscreen (reflected viewport-fill mode — see the fullscreen property), no-fullscreen-button (hide the corner fullscreen toggle), no-minimap (hide the bottom minimap strip). No-legend (hide the "?" legend pill).

Interaction: plain wheel / two-finger scroll routes by DOMINANT axis with a GESTURE-LEVEL AXIS LOCK (WheelGestureRouter). The FIRST decisive unmodified event classifies the stream — horizontal-dominant (|deltaX| > |deltaY|) locks 'h', vertical-dominant (ties included) locks 'v' — and that lock governs. Every unmodified event arriving within WHEEL_GESTURE_GAP_MS (200ms) of the one. (a real swipe is a stream whose jittery minority events are individually opposite-dominant. This also covers per-event routing leaked them). An 'h' gesture is consumed WHOLE: deltaX pans time.

The small vertical component nudges the lane stack when it overflows the host — it never creeps the page. A 'v' gesture is NEVER consumed, whether the lanes overflow (no preventDefault, no zoom: the page scrolls normally over the chart, its horizontal jitter never pans the chart sideways, and the lane stack scrolls by pointer drag or arrow keys instead). A DECISIVE opposite-axis event mid-gesture. Beating the locked axis by more than WHEEL_AXIS_FLIP_RATIO (2x) with at least WHEEL_AXIS_FLIP_MIN_PX (24px) — re-locks. On the spot (proportional jitter can never clear both thresholds, a genuine direction change, or a chart freshly scrolled under the cursor mid-page-scroll that mis-locked on a jitter event, recovers within one tick). A FRESH/ISOLATED event routes exactly by the per-event dominant-axis table.

All deltas deltaMode-normalized. Ctrl/meta+wheel zooms anchored under the cursor (pixel-precise trackpad deltas apply 1:1. Discrete wheel steps glide ~130ms. Always consumed — never browser page-zoom. The cursor anchor holds while follow-now is engaged too — see followNow). Shift+wheel pans time.

Pointer drag pans both axes (pointer capture). Two-pointer pinch zooms anchored at the pinch midpoint (also while following). Keyboard when focused (tabindex 0): arrows pan (shift = faster), +/- zoom, End = jump to now, Home = jump to the earliest known data. The wheel listener sits on the HOST. Those rules apply over the DOM chrome (live pill, fullscreen toggle, stale note) exactly as over the canvas — a horizontal delta is consumed wherever it lands — and the host + canvas. Carry overscroll-behavior-x: none (HORIZONTAL only).

Pulling further at the left pan boundary never chains. Into the browser's history-back/forward navigation gesture, wheel or touch. This is while the VERTICAL axis stays free to chain page scrolling exactly like the wheel router promises. TOUCH mirrors the same rule via the plot canvas' touch-action: pan-y: a one-finger vertical swipe scrolls the PAGE (the browser claims it and the element stops). A horizontal one-finger drag pans the chart, and two-finger pinch-zoom still belongs to the element (pan-y does not allow browser pinch). The accepted tradeoff is that one-finger vertical LANE-drag is gone on touch (arrow keys and desktop drag are unaffected).

The minimap strip keeps touch-action: none (a pure horizontal-drag control), and chrome buttons keep touch-action: manipulation so taps stay instant. Page-LEVEL containment (html/body) stays the embedding page's own business.

CSS custom properties (dark Scratch Proto defaults. See THEME_DEFAULTS). Timeline-bg — plot background (#0d0f14) (must be OPAQUE — the canvas is opaque for subpixel text AA, so a translucent bg will composite on black, not on the host) --timeline-fg, bar labels / primary (#e8ecf4) --timeline-muted. Axis/lane labels (#6b7280) --timeline-grid — vertical time gridlines (rgba(200,205,216,0.07)) --timeline-hairline — lane separators (rgba(200,205,216,0.10)) --timeline-row-tint. Alternating lane tint (rgba(255,255,255,0.015)) --timeline-now. Now line + live pill (#00e47a) --timeline-emphasis — failed/emphasis accents (#ff5c5c) --timeline-stale.

This is stale-feed note (#f0a500) --timeline-font, canvas + chrome font (JetBrains Mono stack) --timeline-font-size. Px of the Base font size (11) --timeline-cat-lightness — category oklch L 0..1 (0.62) --timeline-cat-chroma. Category oklch chroma (0.11) --timeline-track-height — sub-track height px (18, clamped 10..40) --timeline-track-height-compact. Auto-fit demoted sub-track height px (4, clamped 2..track-height. CSS px — DPR scaling supplies device pixels) --timeline-gutter-width — lane gutter px (0 = auto-size) --timeline-tooltip-bg / --timeline-tooltip-fg — tooltip chrome. Category colors use oklch when supported (hsl fallback).

refreshTheme() re-reads the properties after retheming.

Exports: class TimelineViewElement extends HTMLElement THEME_DEFAULTS — default theme values keyed like the CSS properties Types. TimelineData, TimelineHit, LoadRangeFn, TooltipFn, ColorFn, TimelineLegendEntry {glyph, text} Plus everything re-exported from ui/timeline-view-math.js.

### ui/timeline-view-math.js
The timeline's pure math. No DOM or browser APIs (unit-tested under node). Ui/timeline-view.js is the canvas-bound half that consumes it.

Exports: Data types. TimelineLane {id, label, group?}, TimelineInterval, TimelineSegment {start, end?, kind}, TimelineConnector. TimelineMarker {time, label?, kind?}, TimeView {start, end}, TimeRange {start, end}, IntervalStyle, StyleMap, StylePattern, PackItem, LaneMetrics, LaneLayout, HitRect, CategoryColorOptions, CoverageOptions. toMs(t: number | Date) → number Scale/zoom: timeToX(t, view, width), xToTime(x, view, width), panView(view, dt), zoomView(view, anchor, factor, minSpan?, maxSpan?) (anchor-preserving, span clamped. MIN_SPAN_MS = 2s, MAX_SPAN_MS = 7d), defaultSpanForAspect(hostW, hostH, refSpanMs?) → span ms (the aspect-scaled DEFAULT window.

DEFAULT_SPAN_REF_MS = 3 min at 16:9, linear in the container aspect, clamped to the span limits.

Degenerate sizes fall back to the reference), wheelDeltaToPixels(delta, deltaMode, lineHeight?, pageHeight?) (deltaMode 0/1/2 → px), zoomFactorForWheel(deltaPx) (exponential, composable, ZOOM_PX_PER_DOUBLE px per doubling), routeWheel(WheelInput, lanesOverflow) → WheelRoute {zoomPx, panPx, laneScrollPx, consumed} (the PER-EVENT router. Exact for a fresh/isolated event: ctrl/meta = zoom, always consumed. Shift = time pan. Else the DOMINANT axis decides — horizontal-dominant (|dx| > |dy|) pans time, consumed, with the small deltaY nudging lanes only when they overflow. Vertical-dominant incl. ties routes NOWHERE regardless of overflow, and consumed=false means DO NOT preventDefault, let the page scroll. deltaMode normalized), classifyWheel(WheelInput) → WheelClass 'zoom' | 'pan' | 'passthrough' (the per-event routing decision without magnitudes, normalized the same way.

lanesOverflow deliberately has no input — a test-pinned invariant guarantees routeWheel(e, o).consumed === (classifyWheel(e) !== 'passthrough') for ALL inputs and overflow), class WheelGestureRouter. This is route(WheelInput, lanesOverflow, ts) → WheelRoute (the STREAM-level router the element feeds every wheel event through. The first decisive unmodified event locks the gesture's axis — 'h' consumes every unmodified event, dx pans / overflow-gated dy lane-scrolls. 'v' consumes nothing — until unmodified events pause longer than the gap. Otherwise. A mid-gesture event beats the locked axis by more than WHEEL_AXIS_FLIP_RATIO with at least WHEEL_AXIS_FLIP_MIN_PX.

And re-locks on the spot. Ts is the caller's clock (e.timeStamp), not Date.now(). A FRESH router equals routeWheel on any single event — test-pinned. Modifier events delegate to routeWheel and neither read nor extend the lock. Zero-delta unmodified ticks are inert), WHEEL_GESTURE_GAP_MS (200 — unmodified-wheel silence that ends a gesture), WHEEL_AXIS_FLIP_RATIO (2), WHEEL_AXIS_FLIP_MIN_PX (24. The decisive-flip thresholds, both required, on normalized pixels), clampViewToNow(view, now) → TimeView (the hard right end stop: a user view's end never passes now, span preserved), followAfterGesture(wasFollowing, prevEnd, next, now, isPan, msPerDevicePx) → boolean (the follow rule: a backward pan always disengages.

While already following anything else stays pinned — zooming at the live edge keeps following. Re-engage only when the right edge lands within FOLLOW_SNAP_DEVICE_PX (2) DEVICE pixels of the now end stop — pass span / (plotWidthCss * dpr). Do this while not following. FOLLOW_LEAD_FRAC is the pinned lead), followLeadAt(fromFrac, targetFrac, elapsedMs, tweenMs) → number (the eased follow lead, fractions of span. FOLLOW_LEAD_FRAC easeOutQuad, monotone, no overshoot, per-tick step bounded by |target-from|*2*dt/tween, lands exactly on the target at elapsed >= tween. tweenMs <= no snaps — the reduced-motion path.

FOLLOW_LEAD_TWEEN_MS (200) eases engage/disengage, JUMP_TO_NOW_TWEEN_MS (250) the jump/pill glide. And the stale<->fresh live-edge transition), gestureLeadFrac(endMs, now, span, maxFrac) → number (the lead a gesture legitimately holds. (end-now)/span capped at maxFrac — a gesture consumes lead, and never mints it. This also covers seeds both lead easings), snapViewToDevicePixels(view, plotWidthCss, dpr) → TimeView (origin snapped to whole device pixels, span preserved — the global rounding that makes scrolling translate the scene in integer device-pixel steps), snapTextOrigin(v, dpr) → number (a CSS-px coordinate snapped to the nearest whole device pixel. For TEXT draw origins only, where per-element rounding is crispness, not jiggle. Never round bar geometry per element), nowLineX(now, view, gutterX, plotWidthCss, dpr) → number (the now line's snapped x, computed against the RAW view.

This happens while follow-now pins the view the result is frame-to-frame CONSTANT. The snapped render view's per-frame quantization error will wiggle it between adjacent device pixels. It lands on the half-device-px grid for a crisp 1px stroke. This also covers the viewport-anchored exception to the global rounding policy). Staleness: STALE_AFTER_DEFAULT_MS (10_000), feedIsStale(now, lastFresh, staleAfterMs) → boolean (never stale before any data or with a non-finite/non-positive threshold. Strictly-past-threshold trigger), liveEdgeTarget(now, lastFresh, staleAfterMs) → number (the live edge all live semantics advance to: now while fresh, FROZEN at lastFresh once stale — ongoing bars never extrapolate a dead feed).

The tier budget is a hard floor so the chart never renders faster than the tier pacing.
